q: The ratio of change in volume to the original volume is called:
explanation: Volumetric strain = change in volume / original volume, by definition.

q: A simply supported beam as shown carries 10 t of load, 2 m from support A and 3 m from support B. What will be the reaction at point B?
explanation: RB = (Load × distance from A) / span = (10×2)/5 = 4 t.

q: When a rectangular beam is loaded transversely the maximum compressive stress is developed on the:
explanation: For a typical sagging beam, the top fiber experiences maximum compressive stress.

q: A simply supported beam of span L carries a uniformly distributed load W. The maximum bending moment, M is:
explanation: M_max = WL/8 for a full-span UDL (W = total load) on a simply supported beam.

q: Fatigue is the failure of a material under:
options: constant loads but occasionally well above static load
varying loads well below ultimate static load
constant loads well below ultimate static load
varying loads well above ultimate static load
explanation: Fatigue failure occurs from repeated/varying stress cycles, even when each individual cycle's stress is well below the material's ultimate static strength.

q: If a rod is simultaneously pulled at both of its ends, it will be a case of:
explanation: Equal and opposite pulling forces along the rod's axis constitute axial (tensile) loading.

q: A member which does not regain its original shape after the load producing deformation is removed, is said to be:
explanation: Irrecoverable deformation after unloading is the defining characteristic of plastic behavior.

q: The law which states that within elastic limits strain produced is proportional to stress producing it is known as:
explanation: This is the direct statement of Hooke's Law.

q: The ratio of the largest load in a test to the original cross-sectional area of the piece is called:
explanation: Ultimate (tensile) stress is defined as the maximum load reached divided by the original cross-sectional area.

q: The bending moment at a section tends to bend or deflect the beam and internal stresses resist its bending. The resistance offered by the internal stress to the bending, is called:
explanation: The internal normal stress that resists bending action is called bending stress.

q: Tensile internal force tends to:
explanation: Tensile force pulls the member apart, causing elongation.

q: The magnitude of a shear force at a distance of L/4 from either end of a simply supported beam with load P applied at mid span is equal to:
explanation: Between each support and the mid-span load, the shear force stays constant and equal to the support reaction, P/2.

q: Bending moment diagram of a simply supported beam with a point load at the centre of the span is:
explanation: BM rises linearly from zero at the supports to a peak under the central point load, forming a triangle.

q: Stress may be defined as force per unit:
explanation: Stress = Force / Area, by definition.

q: The unit failure stress is taken as:
explanation: For design purposes, the ultimate stress is conventionally used as the reference 'failure' stress of the material.

q: Moment of inertia of an object having rectangular section of 'b' as width and 'd' as depth is given by
explanation: Standard formula: I = bd³/12 about the centroidal axis.

q: Hooke's law holds good up to:
explanation: Hooke's Law (linear stress-strain proportionality) is valid only up to the proportional/elastic limit.

q: The velocity of a moving body is:
explanation: Velocity has both magnitude and direction, making it a vector quantity.

q: The forces which meet at one point but their lines of action do not lie in a plane, are called:
explanation: Forces meeting at a single point (concurrent) but spread across different planes (non-coplanar) are non-coplanar concurrent forces.

q: The tension in a cable supporting a lift:
options: is more when the lift is moving downwards
is less when the lift is moving upwards
Remains constant whether it moves downwards or upwards
is less when the lift is moving downwards
explanation: When a lift accelerates downward, the net upward tension required is less than the static weight (T = m(g − a)).

q: The centre of gravity of a triangle is at the point where three
options: perpendicular bisectors of the sides of the triangle meet
bisectors of the angle of the triangle meet
explanation: The centroid of a triangle is the point where its three medians intersect.

q: The total time of collision and restitution of two bodies, is called
explanation: The combined duration of the compression and restitution phases of a collision is called the period of impact.

q: A cantilever beam is one which is:
options: Fixed at one end and free at other end
Supported on more than two supports
explanation: A cantilever has one fully fixed end and one completely free end.

q: The inclined member carrying compressive load in case of frames and trusses is
explanation: An inclined compression member in a truss/frame is called a strut.

q: A beam is said to be loaded in pure bending when
options: Bending moment and shear force are changing linearly
explanation: Pure bending is characterized by a constant bending moment (and correspondingly zero shear force) over the section of interest.

q: Young's modulus is the ratio of
explanation: Young's Modulus E = longitudinal (axial) stress / longitudinal strain.

q: Mathematically, strain may be defined as
explanation: Linear strain = change in length / original length, i.e. deformation per unit length.

q: If the shear force along a section of a beam is zero, the bending moment at the section is:
explanation: Since dM/dx = V, wherever shear force is zero, bending moment reaches a local extremum — commonly the maximum bending moment for typical loading cases.

q: If a cantilever beam of 8 m long has a uniformly distributed load of 2 KN/m throughout the length and a 10 KN point load at the center of beam, find the moment at center:
explanation: Only the UDL beyond the center (4 m of it, total 8 kN, acting 2 m from center) contributes: 8×2 = 16 kN-m. The point load, applied exactly at the center, has zero moment arm about that same point.
